project.objective: When and where in Ukraine was Wasyl Kapach born, and when did he immigrate to Canada?

questions.question: When and where was Wasyl Kapach born?
questions.rationale: The birth date and place of Wasyl Kapach are unknown and unsourced in the tree. Establishing his birth year and birthplace is the foundational fact for this project — it anchors all downstream research including immigration timing and origin-country record searches. Canadian immigration and naturalization records, death records, and census entries for Wasyl (or his household members) are the primary leads. His birth is a single event with two attributes (date and place), both derivable from the same record types.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All FamilySearch-indexed Canadian collections searched exhaustively for Kapach and Kopach variants: censuses 1901-1931, passenger lists 1881-1922, border entries 1908-1918, homestead files, church records, full-text documents. All returned negative results. Three high-priority sources remain inaccessible in autonomous mode: Alberta Vital Statistics death registration #007-198 (provincial archives), LAC Ukrainian Immigrants 1891-1930 database (interactive), and LAC naturalization records (interactive). The search is exhaustive for autonomously accessible FamilySearch sources but not globally exhaustive.
exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria: Alberta death registration #007-198 examined OR LAC Ukrainian Immigrants database searched OR LAC naturalization records searched

questions.question: When did Wasyl Kapach immigrate to Canada?
questions.rationale: The immigration date is an independent part of the research objective. Canadian passenger lists (available on FamilySearch from approximately 1865 onward), border crossing records, and naturalization papers are the primary sources. Knowing his birthplace (q_001) will help narrow origin-port searches, so q_001 is listed as informing this question's strategy, but the question is independently pursuable via Canadian landing records.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All FamilySearch-indexed Canadian immigration records searched: passenger lists 1881-1922 and border entries 1908-1918. All Canadian censuses 1901-1931 also searched. All returned negative results. LAC Ukrainian Immigrants 1891-1930 database, LAC naturalization records, and Alberta death registration #007-198 remain inaccessible in autonomous mode.
exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria: LAC Ukrainian Immigrants database searched OR LAC naturalization records searched OR Alberta death registration #007-198 examined

items.rationale: Library and Archives Canada's Ukrainian Immigrants 1890–1930 database (https://www.bac-lac.gc.ca/eng/discover/immigration/immigration-records/immigrants-ukraine-1891-1930/Pages/search.aspx) is purpose-built for this question: it indexes Ukrainian immigrant registration records containing name, arrival date, and often the specific village of origin in Galicia or Bukovina — village-level birthplace data unmatched by any other source. Search 'Kapach' and variants (Kopach, Kapac, Kopac). Free to access.

Canada Census 1901 (FamilySearch collection 1584557; 5.3M records, fully indexed). Records birthplace (country/province level), birth year, language spoken, and year of immigration. Ukrainian immigrants who arrived 1896–1900 would appear. Search given-name variants (Wasyl, Wasil, Basil, Vasyl) and surname variants (Kapach, Kapac, Kopach, Kopac). Birthplace column shows 'Austria' or 'Galicia' — not 'Ukraine' — per loc_001 quirk #1. Also on FindMyPast.

Canada, Northwest Provinces, Census, 1906 (FamilySearch collection 1584925; 802K records, fully indexed). Prairie-specific census that captures the main Ukrainian settlement wave of 1896–1905. Records birthplace and year of immigration. Note: this census is filed under 'Northwest Provinces' not provincial titles — per loc_001 quirk #2, pre-1905 Saskatchewan and Alberta records may appear under 'Northwest Territories.' Also available via LAC Census Search portal and Ancestry.

Canada Census 1911 (FamilySearch collection 2143998; 7.2M records, fully indexed). The most genealogically rich prairie census: records birthplace, year of immigration, year of naturalization, and religion. By 1911 the main Ukrainian immigration wave was well underway and most Galician-origin settlers appear. The year-of-immigration column will simultaneously advance q_002. Also available on Ancestry (collection 8947).

Canada, Prairie Provinces, Census, 1916 (FamilySearch collection 1529118; 1.8M records, fully indexed). Prairie-specific mid-decade census capturing immigrants who arrived or relocated after the 1911 enumeration. Records birthplace and year of immigration. Also available on Ancestry (collection 1556). Per loc_001 quirk #3 this census is specific to the prairie provinces and has high value for Ukrainian settlers.

Canada Census 1921 (FamilySearch collection 5000285; 8.6M records, fully indexed). Latest available indexed census; records birthplace, year of immigration, and language. If Wasyl was alive in 1921 this provides a corroborating birthplace statement and may supply more specific geographic detail than earlier censuses. Also available on MyHeritage.

Pre-provided file findagrave-kapach-captures.pdf contains Find a Grave memorial data for the Kapach family. Memorial inscriptions and attached obituary or death-record data may record Wasyl Kapach's birth date and birthplace directly. Family member memorials (Andrew Kapach, Tekla Doliney Kapach, Mary Antosko) may also supply contextual clues about origin. Read the local PDF file — no web access needed.

Canada, Passenger Lists, 1881-1922 (FamilySearch collection 1823240; 3.9M records, fully indexed). Arrival manifests record name, age, last residence (often village-level in Galicia/Bukovina), and destination. Ukrainian immigrants typically traveled Hamburg–Bremen–Liverpool to Canadian ports; the last residence column often names the specific village of origin. This source simultaneously advances q_002. Search all name variants. Also on Ancestry (Canada, Ocean Arrivals 1865-1935, collection 1263).

Canada, Border Entry Lists, 1908-1918 (FamilySearch collection 4123954; 942K records, fully indexed). Some Ukrainian immigrants arrived via US Atlantic ports (Baltimore, Philadelphia, New York) and crossed into Canada by land. These lists state birthplace. Fallback if no ocean passenger arrival is found in pli_008.

Library and Archives Canada holds naturalization declarations and certificates. Ukrainian immigrants naturalized after 5 years of residence (pre-1914 rule); Wasyl likely naturalized ca. 1901–1915. These records frequently state the applicant's exact birth date and village of origin — often more specific than census birthplace entries, which record only country or province. Access via LAC online catalogue (search RG6 series) or written request. Per loc_001, naturalization records are among the richest sources for pinning exact birthplace villages.

Volume_search returned 8,450+ Saskatchewan homestead file volumes, full-text searchable (FamilySearch Canada, Saskatchewan Provincial Records collection id 1916143; 1.5M browse-only images, fulltextSearchable true). Ukrainian homesteaders almost universally filed homestead applications 1896–1914. Application correspondence states country of origin and often the home district or village in Europe. Search 'Kapach' via full-text across these volumes. Also a FAN source: search for other Kapach or Doliney homesteaders who may have settled near Wasyl and share the same origin village.

Canada Passenger Lists 1881-1922 (FamilySearch collection 1823240) and Canada Border Entry Lists 1908-1918 (collection 4123954) were searched in pl_001 items pli_008 and pli_009 respectively — both returned negative results for all Kapach/Kopach surname variants. These searches are complete and are documented here for the q_002 audit trail. Wasyl Kapach does not appear in any indexed FamilySearch immigration record.

Library and Archives Canada's Ukrainian Immigrants 1891-1930 database (bac-lac.gc.ca) indexes Ukrainian immigrant registration records with name, arrival date, and often village of origin. This was deferred in pl_001 (pli_001 logged as deferred, log_001) due to requiring interactive access. This database is the single highest-priority outstanding source for q_002 — it was purpose-built for Ukrainian immigrants arriving in exactly this period. Must be searched in an interactive session.

LAC naturalization records (RG6 series, bac-lac.gc.ca) frequently state the applicant's arrival date in Canada — often more specifically than census immigration columns. Wasyl likely naturalized circa 1901-1915 (Ukrainian settlers typically naturalized after 5 years' residence). This was deferred in pl_001 (pli_010, log_011) as requiring interactive access. Must be searched in an interactive session.

Alberta Vital Statistics death registration #007-198 (cited on Find a Grave memorial) routinely includes a 'year of immigration' or 'years in Canada' field on 1948-era Alberta death registrations. Requesting this record from Service Alberta (Alberta Vital Statistics, Edmonton) would simultaneously address both q_001 (birthplace) and q_002 (immigration date). Physical/correspondence request only; not online.

Outcome partial: birth year 1879 established from gravestone photo (photographed evidence) and corroborated by obituary age statement; birthplace unknown. Alberta death registration #007-198 is a high-priority lead — death records often state country/province of birth. User-contributed memorial — treat 1879 as a lead requiring corroboration from original records.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Birth of Wasyl Kapach

### Research Question

When and where was Wasyl Kapach (FamilySearch tree person L17M-W4Q) born?

### Birth Year — Probable: approximately 1879

The Find a Grave memorial #113540812 for Wasyl 'William' Kapach (src_001) contains two corroborating assertions supporting birth year 1879:

1. **Gravestone inscription** (a_003): A photograph attached to the memorial shows a joint headstone reading 'MARIA 1893 — 1966 | WASYL 1879 — 1948.' The birth year 1879 is thus a *direct* assertion on a *secondary* source — engraved post-death by an unknown informant drawing on family knowledge. No birth month or day is given, and no birthplace is inscribed.

2. **Obituary age statement** (a_004, a_005): The Edmonton Journal obituary of 7 December 1948 states that William Kapach 'passed away ... at the age of 69 years' on December 5, 1948. Subtracting 69 from 1948 yields birth year ~1879, consistent with the gravestone. This is *indirect, secondary* evidence — the obituary writer (likely family) knew the approximate age but not necessarily the exact birth date.

**Correlation and independence:** Both items derive from the same underlying source complex — the memorial and its attached obituary, both compiled after Wasyl's death in December 1948 from family-supplied information. They are therefore *not independent* and constitute one evidence unit, not two. The corroboration is genuine but not confirmatory in the GPS sense; it reflects a single chain of secondary information transmission.

**Confidence tier:** *Probable.* Two secondary, same-source items converge on 1879 with no conflicting evidence. The primary original record — Alberta Vital Statistics death registration #007-198, cited on the memorial — has not been examined. Death registrations routinely record birth date and birthplace supplied by an informant (often a close relative), typically more reliable than post-hoc gravestone inscriptions. Until that record is examined, the GPS standard (Element 1, reasonably exhaustive search) cannot be declared fully satisfied, and the conclusion remains provisional at the 'probable' tier.

### Birthplace — Unresolved

No source in this research project states, implies, or corroborates any birthplace for Wasyl Kapach. The Find a Grave memorial, the gravestone photograph, and the Edmonton Journal obituary are all silent on birthplace. All indexed Canadian census records (1901, 1906, 1911, 1916, 1921, 1931), passenger lists, border entry lists, homestead files, church records, and full-text document searches returned either zero results or clearly non-matching individuals. The expected census birthplace entries ('Austria,' 'Galicia,' or a specific province) that would at minimum establish the origin country were never found because Wasyl does not appear in any accessible indexed census.

### Outstanding Sources

The following sources are required to complete the answer and satisfy the GPS standard:

| Source | Expected contribution | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Alberta Vital Statistics death reg. #007-198 | Birth date; birth country/province (informant typically close family) | Physical request: Service Alberta, Edmonton |
| LAC Ukrainian Immigrants 1891–1930 database | Arrival date; village of origin in Galicia/Bukovina | Interactive: bac-lac.gc.ca |
| LAC naturalization records, RG6 series | Exact arrival date; birthplace; witnesses | Interactive: bac-lac.gc.ca |

Until at least the Alberta death registration is examined, this proof summary remains provisional.

## Immigration Date of Wasyl Kapach

### Research Question

When did Wasyl Kapach (FamilySearch tree person L17M-W4Q) immigrate to Canada?

### Conclusion: Not Proved

No source examined in this project states or implies a specific immigration date for Wasyl Kapach. All indexed FamilySearch immigration and arrival records returned negative results:

- Canada Passenger Lists 1881–1922 (collection 1823240): zero results for Kapach or Kopach variants matching Wasyl's profile
- Canada Border Entry Lists 1908–1918 (collection 4123954): zero results

Canadian census records (1901–1931) that routinely include a 'year of immigration' column were also all negative — Wasyl does not appear in any indexed census.

### Circumstantial Bounds (Indeterminate Quality)

Two contributor-entered assertions provide circumstantial upper bounds on the immigration date:

- **a_010**: Marriage to Maria Antosko ~1909 (contributor-entered, indeterminate quality). If accurate and the marriage occurred in Canada, immigration must predate 1909.
- **a_022**: Daughter Ann born ~1911 (contributor-entered, indeterminate quality). If accurate and born in Canada, immigration must predate 1911.

These bounds cannot sustain a GPS-standard conclusion without corroboration from original records.

### Outstanding Sources Required

| Source | Expected contribution | Access |
|---|---|---|
| LAC Ukrainian Immigrants 1891–1930 database | Arrival date; ship; port; village of origin | Interactive: bac-lac.gc.ca |
| LAC naturalization records, RG6 series | Arrival date stated by applicant | Interactive: bac-lac.gc.ca |
| Alberta Vital Statistics death reg. #007-198 | May include 'years in Canada' field | Physical: Service Alberta |

This question cannot be resolved from the sources accessible in an autonomous FamilySearch-based research session and requires an interactive session targeting LAC databases and/or a physical request to Alberta Vital Statistics.

quirks: Ukrainian immigrants 1891-1914 appear on records as 'Austrian,' 'Russian,' 'Galician,' 'Ruthenian,' or 'Bukovinian' — rarely as 'Ukrainian.' Search all variants.

Alberta and Saskatchewan records before 1 September 1905 are filed under 'Northwest Territories' (District of Alberta / District of Saskatchewan). Search both territorial-era and provincial-era place names — they form one continuous record trail.
The LAC database 'Immigrants from Ukraine (1890-1930)' at bac-lac.gc.ca is the most targeted resource for Ukrainian immigrant ancestors by name and should be the first external-site search.

The 1901 census records both birthplace AND language spoken at home — a birthplace of 'Austria' or 'Russia' plus home language 'Ruthenian' or 'Ukrainian' confirms ethnic identity and narrows the origin region.
Naturalization records (LAC, 1915-1951) frequently contain exact birth date, birthplace village, and year of arrival — often the best single source for both q_001 and q_002.
Homestead records (Saskatchewan, Alberta, Manitoba) often state country of origin and year of arrival — a useful secondary immigration-date source when passenger lists fail.
Saskatchewan court naturalization records (FamilySearch catalog) are images only, not name-indexed — must browse by judicial district (Regina, Yorkton, Saskatoon, Swift Current, Maple Creek).
Saskatchewan Provincial Records 1879-1987 (FS collection 1916143): 1.5M browse-only images containing homestead, land, and provincial records — use fulltext_search on volume numbers.
Saskatchewan homestead files (8,450+ volumes on FamilySearch) are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable via fulltext_search.
Ukrainian surname 'Kapach' may appear as Kapatch, Kapac, Kopach, Kapak, or other anglicizations — broaden spelling in all searches.
Civil birth registration in Alberta began 1898; in Saskatchewan with provincial status in 1905. Church registers are primary substitutes for earlier events.

Ukrainian church registers (Greek Catholic, Orthodox) from small prairie parishes often remain at local parishes or diocesan archives, not digitized — contact the Ukrainian Canadian Research and Documentation Centre (ucrdc.org) for leads.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Canadian Prairie Provinces — Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta (1880–1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Manitoba:** Province since 1870. Pop. 66,000 (1881) → 663,000 (1929).
- **Saskatchewan:** Province since 1905; before that, District of Saskatchewan, Northwest Territories (1882–1905). Pop. 25,700 (1901) → 867,000 (1929).
- **Alberta:** Province since 1905; before that, District of Alberta, Northwest Territories (1882–1905). Pop. 65,900 (1901) → 646,000 (1929).
- **Ukrainian settlement context:** ~170,000 Ukrainians arrived 1891–1914 primarily from Galicia and Bukovina (Austro-Hungarian Empire); second wave in 1920s–30s from Polish/Romanian-governed territories. Alberta: block settlement NE of Edmonton (Beaverhill Lake, Whitford Lake, Willingdon, Vegreville, Vermillion). Saskatchewan: NW from Calder (MB border); Wakaw, Hafford. Manitoba: north of Winnipeg along CNR line.

## Boundary changes
- Alberta and Saskatchewan before 1 September 1905 were Northwest Territories districts — records filed under NWT, not the province name. Search both eras as one continuous trail.
- Manitoba: stable throughout period.

## Census records (highest priority)
- 1881, 1891, 1901, 1911, 1921 — all Canada, indexed + images on FamilySearch.
- 1906, 1916, 1926 — Prairie Provinces only, indexed + images on FamilySearch.
- 1901 and 1911 censuses record birthplace AND language spoken at home — critical for identifying Ukrainian immigrants who list birthplace as 'Austria' or 'Russia'.

## Immigration and passenger records (highest priority for immigration date)
- **Canada Passenger Lists, 1881–1922** (FS 1823240): Quebec, Halifax, Saint John — indexed + images.
- **Canada Border Entry Lists, 1908–1918** (FS 4123954): Land-border crossings from US into Canada — indexed + images.
- **Canada Immigration Records, 1919–1924** (FS 3875202): Ocean arrivals (Form 30A) — indexed + images.
- **LAC Ukrainian Immigrants 1890–1930 database** (bac-lac.gc.ca/eng/discover/immigration/immigration-records/immigrants-ukraine-1891-1930): Most targeted resource — searchable by name.
- **LAC Naturalization Records, 1915–1951**: Often contain exact birth date, birthplace village, and arrival year.

## Church records
- Alberta Catholic Parish Registers, 1865–1916 (FS 2333650): indexed.
- Saskatchewan Catholic Church Records, 1846–1957 (FS 2001071): indexed.
- Manitoba Church Records, 1800–1959 (FS 1992433): indexed.
- Ukrainian Greek Catholic / Orthodox parish registers: many undigitized; contact ucrdc.org.

## Land and homestead records
- Alberta Homestead Records, 1870–1930 (Ancestry $); Saskatchewan Homestead files (8,450+ volumes on FS, full-text searchable); Manitoba/SK/AB Homestead Grant Registers 1872–1930 (Ancestry $).
- Homestead applications often state country of origin and year of arrival.

## Vital records
- Alberta: civil registration from 1898; indexes at Provincial Archives and Ancestry ($).
- Saskatchewan: eHealth Saskatchewan (free index); MyHeritage/Ancestry ($).
- Manitoba: vitalstats.gov.mb.ca (free); Ancestry/Findmypast ($).

## Probate / court records
- Saskatchewan Probate Estate Files, 1887–1931 (FS 1918293): indexed.
- Manitoba Probate Records, 1871–1930 (FS 1987562): indexed.
- Saskatchewan court naturalization records: browse-only by judicial district (catalog entries on FamilySearch).

## Cemetery records
- Saskatchewan Cemetery Transcripts, 1850–1994 (FS 2258205): indexed.
- Find a Grave, BillionGraves, CanadaGenWeb Cemetery Project for all three provinces.

## Research tips
1. Search 'Austrian,' 'Galician,' 'Ruthenian,' 'Bukovinian' as birthplace/ethnicity — not 'Ukrainian.'
2. LAC Ukrainian Immigrants 1890–1930 database is the first external-site search to run.
3. Naturalization records (LAC) are often the best single source for both birth date/place and immigration year.
4. Pre-1905 records for AB and SK: search 'Northwest Territories' — same record trail, different place name.
5. 'Kapach' spelling variants: Kapatch, Kapac, Kopach, Kapak — broaden searches.
6. Homestead records state country of origin and sometimes year of arrival — strong secondary immigration-date source.
